correctness.rationale: The initial-segment map is injective and preserves self-cardinality and min-intersection cardinality, so the F2 orthogonality upper bound is sound. Each of the ten displayed 6-coordinate words has odd sum and each of its 45 pairwise min-intersections has even sum; zero-padded disjoint blocks prove the all-n lower bound with all quantifiers. At n<=5 the compatibility graph has all (3^n-1)/2 candidate vertices, and strictly increasing clique recursion enumerates each possible admissible family once; exact exhaustive zero counts at next size prove the first-five maxima. The verifier independently checks all compatibility tests via bitmask set-intersections. Computations are finite; no unproved asymptotic exactness is asserted.

value.rationale: The question is the direct Oddtown analogue for bounded multiplicities with the canonical minimum-based intersection. A first strict break of the n bound at 4 coordinates and a reusable 6-coordinate block yielding asymptotic density at least 5/3 distinguish the phenomenon structurally from ordinary Oddtown. Exact first-five values identify the minimal obstruction and give a reproducible base of a natural unfinished extremal programme. The ordinary-set bound and finite counts are not inflated into a solved general maximum.
